Not enough data to compare yet
After a few more weeks of matches, we'll point out what's changed from your usual.

Other modes only show K/D, KDA and headshot rate. Round counts, weapons and economy rules differ from Competitive and Unrated, so the other stats can't be measured the same way. Modes with very different rules, like Deathmatch and Team Deathmatch, aren't in your report and only show up in the Matches tab.
No matches in the past %1$d weeks
Once you've played %1$d matches in the past 4 weeks, we'll make your report.
Matches from modes with very different rules, like Deathmatch, aren't in your report (%1$d left out). You can see them in the Matches tab.
Load your recent matches again and we'll make your report.
Your average combat score per round. It builds up from kills, damage and assists.
How many enemies you kill for each death.
When your own ability kills you or a teammate, it doesn't count as a kill. If it kills you, it counts as a death.
How many kills plus assists you get for each death. Unlike K/D, assists count too.
We don't work out KDA for each match first. We add up all your kills, assists and deaths, then divide.
The average damage you deal to enemies per round. Damage that didn't lead to a kill counts too.
The share of your hits that landed on the head. It's not the same as the share of your kills that were headshots.
We don't work out the rate for each match first. We add up all your hits, then divide.
The vertical line marks where the act changed.
See the last 8 weeks at a glance
The red bars are your report period. Tap a bar to see that week's value.
The red bars are your report period, and the horizontal line is your %1$d-week average. Tap a bar to see that week's value.
Over the last %1$d weeks, your weekly value was between %2$s and %3$s.
Over the last %1$d weeks, it stayed at %2$s every week.
Once you have %1$d or more weeks of matches this act, we'll show your usual range.
The share of rounds where you got a kill or an assist, survived to the end, or died but got traded right away by your team.
The share of rounds you survived until the round ended.
Of the rounds where you got the first kill, the share your team won. First kills by your teammates aren't included.
How often you're in a round's opening duel. It's your first kills plus first deaths, divided by rounds played.
How often you win the opening duels you're in. It's your first kills divided by your first kills plus first deaths.
How many assists you get per round.
The share of eco rounds you won. An eco round is one where your team's loadout value averages under 2,000 creds per player. Pistol rounds aren't included.
The share of force buy rounds you won. A force buy round is one where your team's loadout value averages at least 2,000 but under 3,900 creds per player. Pistol rounds aren't included.
The share of rounds played where you killed two or more enemies. It shows whether you kept going after winning one fight and took down the next enemy too.

The share of your deaths where your team killed your killer within 5 seconds. It shows whether you died on your own or while fighting alongside your team. How closely your team followed you up is part of it too.
The share of full buy rounds you won. A full buy round is one where your team's loadout value averages 3,900 creds or more per player. Pistol rounds aren't included.
The count above is what this rate is based on. We only compare when this period and every week we compare it with meet the minimum (%1$s).
We marked this as changed because it moved more than %2$s times your usual week-to-week swing over the last %1$d weeks.
This change is within your usual week-to-week swing, so we didn't mark it as changed.
There isn't enough data from this period or the weeks before it, so we haven't judged whether it changed.
K/D is left blank because you have no deaths. Showing your kill count as is would make it look higher than it really is.
KDA is left blank because you have no deaths. Showing your kills and assists as is would make it look higher than it really is.
%2$s in %1$s is %4$s %5$s than in the %3$s when playing back-to-back.
